text.p01: For every little one brave enough to rest. A story about listening to your body.
text.p03: In golden autumn, little bear Tumble tumbled everywhere: down hills, through leaves, over logs.
text.p04: The forest was getting ready for the Last Leaf Games!
text.p05: Then, deep in his throat, something went tickle, tickle, hack-hack!
text.p06: "A Tickle Monster is inside me!" gasped Tumble. "I must fight it!"
text.p07: Tumble roared at his shadow. He raced the wind and climbed the tallest rock.
text.p08: Hack-hack! Fighting looked so strong. Didn't it?
text.p09: By afternoon, Tumble felt tired and sniffly.
text.p10: Zuzu the bee buzzed around his nose. "Maybe the monster loves it when you race," she said.
text.p11: Mama Bear did not say what to do. She only asked, "Tumble, what does your body need right now?"
text.p12: He had never asked it before.
text.p13: In the cozy den, Tumble listened. His body whispered, "Warm… slow…"
text.p14: So he chose soup, sweet berries, and a soft blanket.
text.p15: Zuzu flew in with a gift from the hive. Mama stirred honey into warm milk.
text.p17: Outside, the games began. Tumble wanted to go so much!
text.p18: But he stayed in, and he coughed into his elbow to keep his friends well.
text.p19: At night, under the moon, Mama whispered, "Your body is the brave one.
text.p20: It is fighting while you sleep. You are helping it."
text.p21: In the morning, the cough was soft and Tumble felt warm and strong.
text.p22: He had not beaten a monster. He had taken care of himself.
text.p23: First snow fell, and Tumble joined the very last game. When a friend coughed, he shared his honey cup.
text.p24: Warm, slow, honey-glow. The strongest bears are gentle with themselves. The End
text.cover: Tumble and the Honey Glow. A Story About Listening to Your Body
